name: LTE cells
label: LTE
notes: LTE base stations (E-UTRA downlink), decoded by OnAir's receiver through the onair-rx handler; the row has no decoder of its own, so only a handler runs it. It reads what each cell broadcasts, not traffic: the cell search, the MIB and the system information. Each event is a cell, first when it is found and again when a member changes: `freq_hz` (the raster frequency: the nearest channel of TS 36.101's table, else the 100 kHz grid), `pci` (the physical cell id; a cell whose MIB is not read yet has `freq_hz` and `pci` only), `bandwidth_hz` (the MIB's), `mcc`, `mnc` (numbers), `tac` and `cell_id` (once SIB1 is read), `sibs` (the SIB numbers decoded so far) and `snr_db`. Nothing is decrypted. The handler takes 20 MHz of IQ, OnAir's usual: it holds a carrier of any width whole, so the system information of a 20 MHz cell is read as well as a 5 MHz one's (a 5 MHz cell needs 4.6 MHz of input at the least), and a job on a narrower band is resampled up to it. Each system information message goes to a packet capture as GSMTAP (type 13, LTE RRC) in IPv4 and UDP to port 4729 (link type 101). Ranges and bands: the spans are the downlink columns of 3GPP TS 36.101's E-UTRA operating bands below 4 GHz (Table 5.5-1), neighbouring bands merged (which bridges the unassigned 1920 to 1930 MHz), across regions; carriers are 1.4 to 20 MHz wide. **The entry runs onair-rx with `--drop`, so a replay can miss**: OnAir's LTE search takes about 2.8 s for each 0.2 s of input at 20 MHz on the build host (0.8 s at 4.6 MHz), so without `--drop` the job would fall behind real time; with it the receiver decodes the blocks it has time for (about one in fourteen) and reads a cell that stays on the air within a few blocks. A replay faster than real time (a capture read from a file) loses most of its input under `--drop`; `capture_decode` replays paced in real time, where it reads the cell. Listing bar: measured on the build host (12 cores) through a scratch node's release build, 30 s of the generated capture looping on a file source and fed in real time; the job skipped no input, onair-rx used 1.08 of a core and the node 0.45 of a core (load average 4.8 to 4.2). Measured on OnAir's 5 MHz cell and on its 20 MHz cell (1.08 of a core each, load 4.1 to 4.2), both input at 20 MHz, with `--drop` (without it the receiver cannot keep real time here).
